469:     def _use_signal(self, fragment: Fragment, signal: _ast.Signal):
470:         """Marks a signal as used in a given fragment.
471: 
472:         Also marks a signal as used if it has to be routed through a given fragment to get from
473:         one part of hierarchy to another.  For this purpose, the ``self.signal_lca`` dictionary
474:         is maintained: for every signal, it stores the topmost fragment in which it has been
475:         marked used so far.
476:         """
477:         if signal in self.fragments[fragment].used_signals:
478:             return
479:         self.fragments[fragment].used_signals[signal] = None
480:         if signal not in self.signal_lca:
481:             # First time we see a signal.
482:             self.signal_lca[signal] = fragment
483:             return
484:         # Signal already seen — go from current fragment to the LCA, marking everything along
485:         # the way as used.
486:         lca = self.signal_lca[signal]
487:         # First, go up from our fragment until it is no deeper than current LCA.
488:         while self.fragments[lca].depth < self.fragments[fragment].depth:
489:             fragment = self.fragments[fragment].parent
490:             # Early return if we reach a part of tree where the signal is already marked.
491:             if signal in self.fragments[fragment].used_signals:
492:                 return
493:             self.fragments[fragment].used_signals[signal] = None
494:         # Second, go up from current LCA until it is no deeper than our fragment.
495:         while self.fragments[lca].depth > self.fragments[fragment].depth:
496:             lca = self.fragments[lca].parent
497:             self.fragments[lca].used_signals[signal] = None
498:         # Now, both fragments are at the same depth. Go up from both until the two paths meet.
499:         while fragment is not lca:
500:             lca = self.fragments[lca].parent
501:             self.fragments[lca].used_signals[signal] = None
502:             fragment = self.fragments[fragment].parent
503:             self.fragments[fragment].used_signals[signal] = None
504:         self.signal_lca[signal] = lca

641:     def _assign_names(self, fragment: Fragment, hierarchy: "tuple[str]"):
642:         """Assign names to signals and IO ports used in a given fragment, as well as its
643:         subfragments.
644: 
645:         The signal mapping is set in ``self.signal_names``, and the IO port mapping is set in
646:         ``self.io_port_names``.  Because names are deduplicated using local information only,
647:         the same signal used in a different fragment may get a different name.
648: 
649:         Subfragments may not necessarily have a name. This method assigns every such subfragment
650:         a name, ``U$<number>``, where ``<number>`` is based on its location in the hierarchy.
651: 
652:         Subfragment names may collide with signal names safely in Amaranth, but this may confuse
653:         backends. This method assigns every such subfragment a new name.

655:         Arguments
656:         ---------
657:         hierarchy : tuple of str
658:             Name of this fragment.
659:         """

661:         frag_info = self.fragments[fragment]
662:         frag_info.name = hierarchy
663: 
664:         if fragment.origins is not None:
665:             for origin in fragment.origins:
666:                 if origin in self.elaboratables:
667:                     other_hierarchy = self.fragments[self.elaboratables[origin]].name
668:                     raise DuplicateElaboratable(f"Elaboratable {origin!r} is included twice "
669:                                                 f"in the hierarchy, as {'.'.join(other_hierarchy)} "
670:                                                 f"and {'.'.join(hierarchy)}")
671:                 self.elaboratables[origin] = fragment
672: 
673:         if fragment is self.fragment:
674:             # Reserve names for top-level ports. If equal to the signal name, let the signal share it.
675:             for name, conn, _dir in self.ports:
676:                 frag_info.assigned_names.add(name)
677:                 if isinstance(conn, _ast.Signal) and conn.name == name:
678:                     frag_info.signal_names[conn] = name
679:                 elif isinstance(conn, _ast.IOPort) and conn.name == name:
680:                     frag_info.io_port_names[conn] = name
681: 
682:         for signal in frag_info.used_signals:
683:             if signal not in frag_info.signal_names and signal.name != "": # Private name shouldn't be added.
684:                 frag_info.signal_names[signal] = _add_name(frag_info.assigned_names, signal.name)
685:         for port in frag_info.used_io_ports:
686:             if port not in frag_info.io_port_names:
687:                 frag_info.io_port_names[port] = _add_name(frag_info.assigned_names, port.name)
688: 
689:         for subfragment_index, (subfragment, subfragment_name, subfragment_src_loc) in enumerate(fragment.subfragments):
690:             if subfragment_name is None:
691:                 subfragment_name = f"U${subfragment_index}"
692:             subfragment_name = _add_name(frag_info.assigned_names, subfragment_name)
693:             self._assign_names(subfragment, hierarchy=(*hierarchy, subfragment_name))

610:     def sigspec(self, *parts: '_nir.Net | Iterable[_nir.Net]'):
611:         value = _nir.Value()
612:         for part in parts:
613:             value += _nir.Value(part)
614: 
615:         chunks = []
616:         begin_pos = 0
617:         while begin_pos < len(value):
618:             end_pos = begin_pos
619:             if value[begin_pos].is_const:
620:                 while end_pos < len(value) and value[end_pos].is_const:
621:                     end_pos += 1
622:                 width = end_pos - begin_pos
623:                 bits = "".join(str(net.const) for net in value[begin_pos:end_pos])
624:                 chunks.append(f"{width}'{bits[::-1]}")
625:             else:
626:                 wire, start_bit = self.nets[value[begin_pos]]
627:                 bit = start_bit
628:                 while (end_pos < len(value) and
629:                         not value[end_pos].is_const and
630:                         self.nets[value[end_pos]] == (wire, bit)):
631:                     end_pos += 1
632:                     bit += 1
633:                 width = end_pos - begin_pos
634:                 if width == 1:
635:                     chunks.append(f"{wire.name} [{start_bit}]")
636:                 else:
637:                     chunks.append(f"{wire.name} [{start_bit + width - 1}:{start_bit}]")
638:             begin_pos = end_pos
639: 
640:         if len(chunks) == 1:
641:             return chunks[0]
642:         return "{ " + " ".join(reversed(chunks)) + " }"

708:     def emit_assignment_list(self, cell_idx, cell):
709:         def emit_assignments(case, cond):
710:             # Emits assignments from the assignment list into the given case.
711:             # ``cond`` is the net which is the condition for ``case`` being active.
712:             # Returns once it hits an assignment whose condition is not nested within ``cond``,
713:             # letting parent invocation take care of the remaining assignments.
714:             nonlocal pos
715: 
716:             while pos < len(cell.assignments):
717:                 assign = cell.assignments[pos]
718:                 if assign.cond == cond:
719:                     # Not nested, so emit the assignment.
720:                     case.assign(self.sigspec(lhs[assign.start:assign.start + len(assign.value)]),
721:                                 self.sigspec(assign.value))
722:                     pos += 1
723:                 else:
724:                     # Condition doesn't match this case's condition — either we encountered
725:                     # a nested condition, or we should break out.  Try to find out exactly
726:                     # how we are nested.
727:                     search_cond = assign.cond
728:                     while True:
729:                         if search_cond == cond:
730:                             # We have found the PriorityMatch cell that we should enter.
731:                             break
732:                         if search_cond == _nir.Net.from_const(1):
733:                             # If this isn't nested condition, go back to parent invocation.
734:                             return
735:                         # Grab the PriorityMatch cell that is on the next level of nesting.
736:                         priority_cell_idx = search_cond.cell
737:                         priority_cell = self.netlist.cells[priority_cell_idx]
738:                         assert isinstance(priority_cell, _nir.PriorityMatch)
739:                         search_cond = priority_cell.en
740:                     # We assume that:
741:                     # 1. PriorityMatch inputs can only be Match cell outputs, or constant 1.
742:                     # 2. All Match cells driving a given PriorityMatch cell test the same value.
743:                     # Grab the tested value from a random Match cell.
744:                     test = _nir.Value()
745:                     for net in priority_cell.inputs:
746:                         if net != _nir.Net.from_const(1):
747:                             matches_cell = self.netlist.cells[net.cell]
748:                             assert isinstance(matches_cell, _nir.Matches)
749:                             test = matches_cell.value
750:                             break
751:                     # Now emit cases for all PriorityMatch inputs, in sequence. Consume as many
752:                     # assignments as possible along the way.
753:                     switch = case.switch(self.sigspec(test))
754:                     for bit, net in enumerate(priority_cell.inputs):
755:                         subcond = _nir.Net.from_cell(priority_cell_idx, bit)
756:                         if net == _nir.Net.from_const(1):
757:                             emit_assignments(switch.default(), subcond)
758:                         else:
759:                             # Validate the above assumptions.
760:                             matches_cell = self.netlist.cells[net.cell]
761:                             assert isinstance(matches_cell, _nir.Matches)
762:                             assert test == matches_cell.value
763:                             patterns = matches_cell.patterns
764:                             emit_assignments(switch.case(patterns), subcond)
765: 
766:         lhs = _nir.Value(_nir.Net.from_cell(cell_idx, bit) for bit in range(len(cell.default)))
767:         proc = self.builder.process(src_loc=cell.src_loc)
768:         proc.assign(self.sigspec(lhs), self.sigspec(cell.default))
769:         pos = 0 # nonlocally used in `emit_assignments`
770:         emit_assignments(proc, _nir.Net.from_const(1))
771:         assert pos == len(cell.assignments)
